headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill shifts the cost of grid infrastructure from residential users to large energy users, primarily data centers, and extends energy assistance programs.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocacy groups, low-income individuals.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users.
news_headline: Governor Amends Bills Shifting Data Center Costs.
news_summary: Governor Spanberger signed and suggested changes to HB 1393, a key energy measure designed to shift more costs onto data centers to save residential electricity customers money and expand a power line burial program. Critics argue the governor's amendments weaken the original intent of the bill, which aimed to lower costs for customers and expand energy assistance.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates water suppliers to report data centers' water consumption, increasing transparency and providing data for water resource management.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservationists, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
news_headline: Virginia Lawmakers Approve Data Center Water Use Tracking.
news_summary: The Virginia General Assembly passed SB 553, sponsored by Senator Kannan Srinivasan, to strengthen water-use reporting requirements for data centers. This legislation aims to provide better data on the amount of water supplied to data centers, addressing concerns about the industry's impact on Virginia's water resources.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill requires site assessments for noise impacts and allows localities to demand information on potential impacts to water, agriculture, forests, and parks for new data center developments.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups.
news_headline: New Virginia Law Governs Data Center Siting and Disclosures.
news_summary: Virginia's new law, HB 153, requires developers of large data centers to conduct site assessments for noise impacts on residential areas and schools. It also allows localities to require information on potential impacts to water, agriculture, forests, and parks, though it does not set specific limits on noise or water use.
